identity.name: MIDWEST LIMITED
identity.industry: Minerals & Rare Earths / Quartz & Granite Processing

summary.oneLiner: Midwest has transformed from a granite miner to an integrated materials processor with Phase 1 quartz plant commissioned and Phase 2 + HMS facility funded by IPO proceeds, driving EBITDA margin expansion to 29% and positioning for 2.5x revenue growth by FY29 via rare earths and titanium feedstock — the key shift is from fragmented stone sales to high-margin, strategic raw material supply for solar, semiconductors, and defense.

one-line thesis: Midwest has transformed from a granite miner to an integrated materials processor with Phase 1 quartz plant commissioned and Phase 2 + HMS facility funded by IPO proceeds, driving EBITDA margin expansion to 29% and positioning for 2.5x revenue growth by FY29 via rare earths and titanium feedstock — the key shift is from fragmented stone sales to high-margin, strategic raw material supply for solar, semiconductors, and defense.
financial scorecard: revenue: +8% YoY (INR301cr H1); EBITDA: +16% YoY (INR86cr H1), margin: 28%+ (up from 27% FY25); PAT: +40% YoY (H1), normalized PAT excludes INR25cr one-off elimination gain from disinvested subsidiary; order book: N/A disclosed; net debt: reduced to ~INR120cr post-IPO debt repayment (from INR170cr pre-IPO)
guidance: revenue growth: >2x from FY25 baseline by FY29; margin: targeting 35%+ ROCE, EBITDA margins to improve with HMS/rare earths; order inflow: LOI from KMLL for monazite pilot; capex/commissioning: Phase 2 quartz (606ktpa) by FY27, HMS plant by FY27, solar CAPEX may slip to FY28
order book & pipeline: LOI from Kerala Mines and Minerals Limited (KMLL) for monazite cracking pilot project; no other order book disclosed
segment / subsidiary detail: Granite: 60% export, 40% domestic (mix shifting); Black Galaxy = 20% of India’s production, 64% of exports; Quartz Phase 1: 303ktpa, 60-70% utilization in H1 FY26; HMS: licensing in Sri Lanka, monazite as byproduct; Diamond Wire: in-house, used for captive + third-party sales
growth verticals / optionality: Phase 2 quartz (HPQ for semiconductors); HMS plant (titanium feedstock); monazite-to-oxide processing via KMLL pilot; potential PLI for rare earths; export expansion of quartz to global solar/engineered stone markets
margins & cost dynamics: Current EBITDA margin 28-29% driven by granite efficiency; quartz margins expected >30%; HMS/rare earths margins targeted at 40-42% (Iluka benchmark); cost advantages from vertical integration, electric trucks (reducing diesel cost), solar power, and low-cost Sri Lanka monazite byproduct
capex / expansion: Total IPO proceeds: INR250cr; allocated to Phase 2 quartz (INR130cr), debt repayment (INR50cr+), solar CAPEX; HMS capex funded internally; Phase 2 quartz capex ~INR125-130cr; total capex to be completed within 12-15 months
capital allocation: IPO proceeds: 50% to Phase 2 quartz, 20% to debt repayment, 30% to solar CAPEX; future HMS capex from internal accruals; no dividend policy disclosed; focus on deleveraging (debt/equity now 0.38x) and high-ROCE projects
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in HMS licensing; monazite processing tech risk; global rare earth price volatility; execution risk on Phase 2 quartz commissioning; cyclone/flood disruptions to mining; KMLL MOU not yet signed
management quality / tone: Highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; repeatedly emphasized ‘world-class’ ambitions; strong emphasis on technology adoption (electric trucks, diamond wire R&D); transparent on one-offs; optimistic on rare earth tailwinds and import substitution
non-obvious takeaways: Monazite from Sri Lanka is a low-cost byproduct of HMS mining — not a standalone cost center; KMLL LOI is a de facto off-take agreement for rare earth oxides; diamond wire manufacturing is a hidden margin enhancer used internally and sold externally; 99-day working capital is exceptional for mining sector

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Over four decades of expertise in dimensional natural stone exploration, mining, processing, and global distribution across 17 countries and 5 continents, with key markets in China, Italy, and Thailand."
- "India's largest Black Galaxy Granite producer & exporter and largest Absolute Black Granite Producer"; the deck notes "Black Galaxy is available in only one village in Andhra Pradesh in the entire world".
- "Exclusive mining rights gives competitive edge in terms of strong revenue visibility" and the company "Serves as an organized player in an otherwise unorganized and fragmented market."
- Claims "India's largest integrated Quartz Processing Plant, supplying raw materials to solar glass and engineered stone manufacturers in domestic and export markets".
- Vision stated as "building leadership in quartz, titanium feedstock and rare earth oxides globally".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [R&D] "8 member dedicated R&D/Exploration team with on an average 16.10 years of industry experience" — 6 Geologists, 1 Chemist, 1 Quality control specialist — focused on tracing new mineral deposits (satellite imagery, geological/geophysical reports) and improving operational efficiency and product quality.
- [Market context] Deck cites CRISIL: "India currently imports 65% of its solar glass needs, but domestic supply is expected to rise to 70-80% by FY 2030" and "Quartz demand for solar glass is expected to grow at a CAGR of 30.7-31.4%, reaching 1,840-2,000 KT by FY 2030".
- [Recognition] "Three Star Export House" awarded by Ministry of Commerce and Industry in 2024 (earlier "Star Export House" 2013-2018 and "One Star Export House" 2015-2020).
- [Governance] Promoter group includes Mr. Kollareddy Rama Raghava Reddy (Founder and President), Mr. Kollareddy Ramachandra (Promoter, Whole-time Director & CEO), Mrs. Uma Priyadarshini Kollareddy (Promoter and Whole-time Director) and Mrs. Kukreti Soumya (Promoter and Non-Executive Director); the extracted director-to-biography mapping in the annexure appears scrambled, so individual bios are not asserted here.
